sub_scenario.family: communicating uncertainty and risk escalation in cross-functional decisions
sub_scenario.one_line: service design researcher: accept only with explicit uncertainty safeguards

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the research notebook and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The interview calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I enjoy facilitating a scheduled interview when the participant's history is in the brief.
Does facilitation itself worry you?
No, a prepared conversation is energizing.
Someone new shadowed me in the insight studio this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the discovery sprint into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
In a vendor complaint review, I committed to a product explanation before I separated interview quotes from our inference, and the team built the wrong follow-up script.
What would you do differently?
I would label the uncertainty before proposing an owner.
I can explain a tentative finding clearly after marking it as observed, inferred, or still open.
Why label it that way?
It keeps the group from treating a hunch as a conclusion.
I archived last cycle's notes on the interview calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My concentration becomes patchier after 14:30, particularly when several people challenge an incomplete story at once.
Can you compensate by preparing?
Preparation helps, but a late live debate still needs a tighter boundary.
A vendor call about the research notebook ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the insight studio checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the discovery sprint.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the interview calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The program manager asks whether I will react well to a 15:30 daily office hour if I can begin with a five-minute evidence check and defer unverified cases.
Would that change your reaction?
I would be willing to try it only with those guardrails.
I sketched next week's plan for the discovery sprint before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the research notebook updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The research calendar leaves a 10:30 slot open for cases that need a deeper evidence review the next day.
Is that relevant?
Yes, it makes deferral a real option rather than a promise.
I compared two options for the interview calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the insight studio handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How am I likely to respond to the proposed 15:30 escalation hour if it includes an evidence check and a next-morning follow-up slot?

replacement_dialogue.content: I filed the routine discovery sprint paperwork and confirmed the owner list.
I did a standard pass over the interview calendar records this morning.
The manager removes the evidence check and requires a definitive owner at the end of every 15:30 conversation.
I would decline because the necessary guardrails are gone.
